run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: No evidence exists in this Run for the cluster the question names: every document in the only log index available, app-264-prod-logs, is labelled cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2 (index total = 3 documents, all three returned for the full authorized window 2026-11-20T06:12:27Z to 2026-11-21T06:12:27Z). Nothing labelled production-eu-west-2 was found, and my Kubernetes access is the staging-eu-west-2 cluster (otel-demo namespace), so I cannot name a root cause for production checkout 500s. The one checkout-service 500 line that does exist is a staging record at 2026-11-21T05:12:19Z ("POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"), accompanied by a second staging checkout-service ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:12:19Z ("Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress") and a staging payment-service WARN at 2026-11-21T05:42:19Z ("Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)"); these describe staging-eu-west-2, not production-eu-west-2, and the staging checkout pod's own logs in otel-demo show successful payments with no error-severity line in the window, so they do not establish a live checkout failure even there. Prometheus and Jaeger tool calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run, so no metric or trace evidence was usable. In the staging cluster I did observe a cluster-wide pod restart at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown on every otel-demo pod) and a crash-looping nginx prometheus-readonly-proxy whose previous container logged "host not found in upstream 'prometheus:9090'" at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z, but neither is tied by evidence to checkout 500s in production-eu-west-2.

claims.text: The log index app-264-prod-logs contains 3 documents in total, and all 3 returned inside the authorized window carry cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2 — no document returned carries production-eu-west-2.

Nothing was found under the exact cluster name production-eu-west-2 in app-264-prod-logs; the documents that exist belong to the similarly named but different cluster staging-eu-west-2: 2026-11-21T05:12:19Z service=checkout-service level=ERROR "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"; 2026-11-21T04:12:19Z service=checkout-service level=ERROR "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress"; 2026-11-21T05:42:19Z service=payment-service level=WARN "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)".

The Kubernetes objects I can read are in the staging-eu-west-2 cluster: deployment otel-demo/checkout is ready=1/available=1 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, and its pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n is Running with restartCount 1 and a last termination of exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z.

In the staging cluster the mass restart is not specific to checkout: all 22 pods of the otel-demo namespace show restartCount 1 with last termination exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (for example ad-757d59f5dd-d4427, cart-549b8757d-zjgcd, frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw), and the node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure since 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn in otel-demo (staging-eu-west-2) shows 3 restarts, and its previous nginx container logged "2026/11/21 04:24:05 [emerg] 1#1: host not found in upstream \"prometheus:9090\" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22" at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z while the current instance had written no lines.

The staging checkout pod's own logs do not show an application error: 3601 lines were read from checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n between 2026-11-20T06:12:27Z and 2026-11-21T06:12:27Z, and a regex search for error|fail|500|exception|panic|refused matched 32 lines that are all info-severity "[PlaceOrder]", "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and "order confirmation email sent" entries (the matches come from digits such as 500 inside UUIDs), i.e. payments were succeeding in staging.

Events in the authorized window do not mention checkout: the 18 events returned across all namespaces (observed 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z to 2026-11-21T06:06:19Z) involve only Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod loki and payment-api-101 in namespace app-101 plus one Warning "Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints 'loki' already exists" at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z.

Rejected: that the two ERROR documents in app-264-prod-logs (the 500 "integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired" line and the "deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress" line) identify the cause of the production-eu-west-2 checkout 500s — both are labelled cluster=staging-eu-west-2/environment=staging, and the staging checkout pod logged successful payments in the same window, so they cannot be attributed to production-eu-west-2.

Hypothesis (unverified): the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z container restart of every otel-demo pod (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) and the 04:24:10Z nginx "host not found in upstream 'prometheus:9090'" failure may be why Prometheus and Jaeger tool calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run; no evidence identifies what triggered the mass restart.

Have a human locate the production-eu-west-2 checkout-service log/metric source: app-264-prod-logs contains only staging-eu-west-2 documents, so check whether production logs are being written to a different index or whether the production pipeline is misrouting into this staging-labelled index, then re-run the 500 investigation against production data.

Restore the observability backends before concluding anything about checkout: Prometheus and Jaeger were unusable in this Run, and the staging nginx sidecar for the read-only Prometheus proxy failed upstream resolution of prometheus:9090, so alert rules, span error rates and latency baselines could not be checked.

gaps: No data for production-eu-west-2: the only log index in this Run (app-264-prod-logs, 3 documents total) contains exclusively cluster=staging-eu-west-2 / environment=staging documents, so the production-eu-west-2 checkout-service 500s are unobserved rather than explained.

Prometheus was unavailable for every call: get_all_labels on {__name__=~"traces_span_metrics_calls_total|kube_pod_owner"}, metrics_range_query sum by (service_name,status_code) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[86400s])), execute_prometheus_instant_query up, and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency baseline or kube-state-metrics series could be read (unknown, not zero).

Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services and traces_search for service checkout (2026-11-21T04:00:00Z-06:12:27Z) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, operation or parent-child evidence was available.

The trigger of the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z restart (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) of all otel-demo pods in staging-eu-west-2 is not identified by the evidence I could read, and it is not tied to any checkout failure.
Events were only readable from 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z to 2026-11-21T06:06:19Z (18 events), so earlier activity in the authorized window, and any event that had expired, is unknown.

Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change record for either cluster could be checked; whether the staging ERROR line "deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress" corresponds to a real rollout is unverified.
No logs of any production checkout pod could be read: Kubernetes access is limited to the staging-eu-west-2 cluster.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
